intro.title: The adaptive topology laboratory
intro.sub: who is seated, how candidates become accepted code, and the experiments that will decide what the team becomes
intro.proseHTML:
Primary audience: you, Brad

This map is decision support first. The experiment districts (south-east) are separate city blocks so arms can be compared at a glance; the two slate diamonds on QA-2 ∥ HLDT and QA-2-first are deferred authorizations that belong to you alone. The acceptance chain (west) is the spine every candidate rides: gates → QA-1 → QA-2 → sealed holdout → commit, all on ONE immutable digest.

Truth discipline

Seats and surfaces are [OBSERVED] live via cmux at 18:59Z. Chain design, stages, and arms come from the session objectives and A/EXEC-ODIN's GO packet. The Wave-1 timeline is observed by A/EXEC-ODIN and cross-checks against the session baselines (9m29 / 28m51, digests 46dea649… / 4668cdd0… agree across both sources). Model assignments arrive via the packet. Sealed-holdout internals are deliberately absent.

How to read it

North: Team A (your executive office, plus two consultants and the display pane). Middle: Team B — control, the tournament cohort, fixers, and the chain. South: the eight experiment arms and the measurement district. Run the trace to ride one candidate (46dea649…) through the whole chain including its failure and repair. Press R for home; click any building for its evidence class.

drcBudget.acknowledged: advisory draft — observed 87 weighted crossings, forced by topology: one router fans out to three lanes; three lanes converge on one gate; a four-role sequential chain carries feedback loops; and the deferred arms intentionally edge toward the exact chain links they propose to reorder. This crossing debt IS the experiment's shape.
